problems.title: Adjacent unmerged transforms omit the transformed residual
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v4 Section 2.2, PDF pp.3–4, Eq.(5); Appendix A.16, PDF pp.23–24; ReplaceMe/lstsq.py, lines 195–246
claim: The fitted full-state target is \((Y+MT_1)T_2\), but the unmerged fusion applies both transforms only to the MLP contribution.
analysis: The fused expression is \(Y+MT_1T_2\), missing \(Y(T_2-I)\). In the scalar three-block example with \(T_1=3\), \(T_2=2\), the result is \(7\) rather than \(8\). The default merged fit uses one residual transform \(7\) and returns \(8\), so this witness does not accuse that default route.
result: The nondefault adjacent-unmerged option is not algebraically equivalent to its fit.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Merge adjacent cuts before fitting, as the passing default does, or explicitly transform the residual contribution. No blanket removal of fusion is justified.
problems.impact_rationale: A nondefault release option fails while the default relevant control passes.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Padding rows change the least-squares calibration target
problems.source_location: Current author ReplaceMe/lstsq.py and ReplaceMe/cosine_dist.py, flattened calibration activation accumulation
claim: The tokenizer supplies an attention mask, but flattened calibration activations enter the fit without masking padded positions.
analysis: Valid scalar rows \((M,B)=(1,1),(2,2)\) fit \(T=1\). Adding a masked row \((1,10)\) changes the unweighted fit to \(T=2.5\), giving valid-row squared error \(11.25\). The model’s attention mask does not automatically exclude a saved padded activation from a later regression.
result: The fit can depend on padding and batching. A deliberate pad-inclusive objective would need to be declared; historical influence is unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Apply the same valid-token mask to every aligned activation tensor, giving weighted regression \(\|W^{1/2}(MT-B)\|_F^2\) with zero weights on padding.
problems.impact_rationale: This is calibration-objective correspondence, without a measured effect on the main results.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The elasticnet branch penalizes activations rather than the matrix
problems.source_location: Section 2.3, p. 4, Eq. (9); Section 3.3.2/Table 5, p. 8; utils.py lines 254–260.
claim: Equation (9) regularizes the transform matrix \(T\). The released `utils.py`, `adam_method`, instead applies its elasticnet-like term to transformed activations.
analysis: With input and target row \((1,0)\), matrices \(\operatorname{diag}(1,1)\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(1,100)\) produce the same transformed row and released loss, approximately \(0.135\), but very different matrix norms. An activation penalty cannot generally implement the stated matrix penalty.
result: The public option does not reproduce that regularization definition. The private ablation implementation is not identified.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Define the matrix regularizer and reduction explicitly and apply it to the matrix. Keep ordinary unregularized cosine and least-squares ridge paths distinct.
problems.impact_rationale: This concerns an ablation/release option; use of the wrong historical objective is not established.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The inverse and sample count require rank and noise conditions
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v4 Eq.(6), PDF p.4; Appendix A.2, PDF p.15; Appendix A.12, PDF p.21
claim: The displayed solution uses \((M^\top M)^{-1}M^\top B\), and the token discussion links a square transform to a quadratic token requirement.
analysis: For \(M=((1,1),(2,2))\), the inverse is undefined although a pseudoinverse gives an exact fit. Conversely, noiseless \(M=I_d\) recovers an arbitrary \(d\)-by-\(d\) transform from \(d\) vector-valued rows, so \(d^2\) parameters do not imply \(d^2\) tokens. No historical singular calibration is established.

Rank-revealing least squares or an explicitly declared ridge estimator specifies behavior beyond the full-rank inverse formula. Algebraic identifiability and statistical accuracy require separate conditions; no historical singular fit is established.
result: Full-column rank, conditioning, noise and dependence assumptions are needed for those interpretations.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a scoped mathematical qualification rather than an established experiment failure.
problems.existing_correction_status: Scope clarification only; no author-paper repair or adoption is asserted.
